### Summary

On the gnomonic cubed sphere the diffusion module of @sec-ch09-viscosity runs a different operator. The panel axes
are not orthogonal and every panel has its own basis, so the module works in Cartesian components: it turns the
velocity into a Cartesian vector, takes its gradient through the discrete map from panel indices to Cartesian
position, and forms the Newtonian stress and the heat flux on every face of the block. Faces on a block edge are
shared with the neighbouring panel through an exchange that makes the two sides carry one flux, so momentum and
energy are conserved across the seams, and a penalty on the jump between the two sides couples the panels. The
radial heat flux can optionally be taken implicitly, split around the explicit step.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The stress, its work and the heat flux of @eq-ch09-viscosity-flux on the cubed sphere, in Cartesian
components; @eq-ch09-csdiffusion-grad, @eq-ch09-csdiffusion-radial.

**Data.** In: velocity, temperature, density and $c_v$ of the block's interior cells; out: covariant momentum and energy tendencies.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, in the forcing loop like the Cartesian module; the optional radial solve runs before stage 0 and after the last stage.

**Activation.** The `diffusion` block of `forcing:` with `nu_iso` or `kappa_iso` $>0$ on `gnomonic-equiangle`; `temperature_inner`, `temperature_outer`, `wall_velocity`, `implicit_radial` default to 0, `stress-free`, `false`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact seam conservation; zero tendency for rigid rotation and for $T=A+B/r$; needs reflecting radial walls and one block in $x_1$.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer: the ctests run at the pin, CPU and CUDA.
:::

**Data details.** In: the primitive state `w` of the block (density $\rho$ [kg m$^{-3}$], contravariant velocity
$v^a$ [m s$^{-1}$]), the temperature $T$ [K] and the mixture $c_v$, at the interior cells only: the operator reads no
ghost cell. The coefficients are $\mu=\nu\rho$ and $K_{\mathrm c}=\kappa\rho c_v$ with the default `dynamic: false`, or
`nu_iso` and `kappa_iso` themselves with `dynamic: true`, times the $x_1$ profiles of @sec-ch09-x1profile when given.
Out: the momentum rows of the increment, lowered to covariant form, and the energy row.

**Evidence details.** Tests: rest and rigid rotation give no tendency, a degree-2 harmonic converges with heat
conserved, $T=A+B/r$ is a discrete equilibrium, the closed-shell heat operator has no growing mode, and the
implicit radial step is second order (@tbl-ch09-csdiffusion-tests). The numbers quoted below come from runs of
`test_diffusion_cubed_sphere` at the pin on CPU and CUDA.[^csd-run]

Local symbols: $\mathbf X$ [m] the Cartesian position of a point; $\mathbf a_j=\partial\mathbf X/\partial x_j$ and
$\mathbf a^j$ the covariant basis of the coordinates $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ (radius [m] and the two panel angles [rad]) and its reciprocal;
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ [-] the unit normal of a face; $\mathbf t$ [Pa] the traction $\boldsymbol\Pi\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}$;
$K_{\mathrm c}$ [W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$] the conductivity, $\kappa\rho c_v$ or $\kappa$; $\Delta n_{\mathrm s}$ [m] the
normal distance between the two cell centres across a block edge; $\mathcal G^{ab}$ [-] the inverse metric of the
equiangular panel on the unit sphere ($a,b\in\{2,3\}$); $b_{\mathrm{SD}}=1-1/\sqrt2$ [-] the stage coefficient of the
radial solve; $\mathsf M$, $\mathsf K$, $\mathbf S$ the heat-capacity matrix, conductance matrix and wall source of
that solve. $\boldsymbol\Pi$ is that of @sec-ch09-viscosity; $\psi$, $h$, $\mu$, $\nu$, $\kappa$, $c_v$,
$g_{ab}$[^rg-aec86920bf13], $v^a$ and $m_a$ are defined in @sec-appa.

The operator is the Cartesian module's physics on another grid. It is chosen by the grid type and needs no switch.
The four wall and radial-solve keys are read on every grid, but only `temperature_inner` and `temperature_outer`
act on a Cartesian grid (@sec-ch09-viscosity). Aliases: cubed-sphere diffusion and its radial SDIRK split.[^csd-src]

[^csd-src]: Source and credit: `chengcli/snapy#324` (cubed-sphere diffusion) and `chengcli/snapy#325` (its
    convergence study, the exchange in four rounds and the two-GPU[^rg-b657d8257123] test).

### Derivation

#### Fluxes in Cartesian components

Write the velocity as a Cartesian vector $\mathbf v(\mathbf X)$. With the stress
$\boldsymbol\Pi=\mu[\nabla\mathbf v+(\nabla\mathbf v)^{\mathsf T}-\tfrac23(\nabla\cdot\mathbf v)\mathsf I]$ of
@sec-ch09-viscosity, the momentum and energy fluxes through a face of unit normal $\hat{\mathbf n}$ are

$$
\mathbf F^{(\mathbf m)} = -\mathbf t,\qquad F^{(E)} = -\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf t - K_{\mathrm c}\,\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\nabla T,
\qquad \mathbf t=\boldsymbol\Pi\cdot\hat{\mathbf n} .
$$ {#eq-ch09-csdiffusion-flux}

This is @eq-ch09-viscosity-flux for an arbitrary face direction. The code stores `flux`[^rg-a2ea0b344b78] as $-\mathbf t$ in the
three momentum rows and the heat flux minus $\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf t$ in the energy row
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}}).

#### The velocity gradient through the discrete map

The cell index directions are the coordinates $x_j$. By the chain rule,

$$
\nabla\mathbf v = \sum_{j=1}^{3}\frac{\partial\mathbf v}{\partial x_j}\otimes\mathbf a^j,\qquad
\mathbf a^1=\frac{\mathbf a_2\times\mathbf a_3}{\mathbf a_1\cdot(\mathbf a_2\times\mathbf a_3)}\ \text{(cyclic)},\qquad
\mathbf a_j=\frac{\partial\mathbf X}{\partial x_j} .
$$ {#eq-ch09-csdiffusion-grad}

The code differentiates the Cartesian velocity and the Cartesian position $\mathbf X=r\,\hat{\mathbf e}_r$ with the
same stencil (`deriv`), forms $\mathbf a^j$ by the cross products and the determinant, and sums the products into
`vg` ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}}). The step that makes
this exact for an affine field takes three lines.

1. Let $\mathbf v=\mathsf A\mathbf X+\mathbf b$ with a constant matrix $\mathsf A$ and vector $\mathbf b$.
2. The stencil is linear and differentiates a constant to zero, so the discrete $\partial_j\mathbf v$ equals
   $\mathsf A$ times the discrete $\partial_j\mathbf X=\mathbf a_j$, with the same weights, in exact arithmetic.
3. Hence $\sum_j\mathsf A\mathbf a_j\otimes\mathbf a^j=\mathsf A\sum_j\mathbf a_j\otimes\mathbf a^j=\mathsf A$,
   because $\mathbf a_j\cdot\mathbf a^l$ is $1$ for $j=l$ and $0$ otherwise by construction of the reciprocal basis.

A rigid rotation $\mathbf v=\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf X$ has an antisymmetric $\mathsf A$, so
$\nabla\mathbf v+(\nabla\mathbf v)^{\mathsf T}=0$ and $\nabla\cdot\mathbf v=0$ hold discretely: no stress, on
every panel. The same argument does not hold for the face trace of $\mathbf v$, because the interpolated position
is not exactly on the curved face; the code adds `vg` times that displacement to the face velocity, which makes the
trace exact for affine fields too ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}}).

#### Face normals

The basis vectors $\hat{\mathbf e}_2$, $\hat{\mathbf e}_3$ along the panel axes have unit length and
$\hat{\mathbf e}_2\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_3=\cos\psi$ (@sec-ch03-gnomonic). The unit normal of a face $x_2=$ const
must be orthogonal to $\hat{\mathbf e}_3$ and to $\hat{\mathbf e}_r$, which gives

$$
\hat{\mathbf n}_2=\frac{\hat{\mathbf e}_2-\cos\psi\,\hat{\mathbf e}_3}{\sqrt{1-\cos^2\psi}},
$$

and $\hat{\mathbf n}_3$ with 2 and 3 swapped; check: $\hat{\mathbf n}_2\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_3=(\cos\psi-\cos\psi)/\sin\psi=0$.
A radial face has $\hat{\mathbf n}_1=\hat{\mathbf e}_r$. The code builds the three unit vectors with `basis` and the
normal as `normal` ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp basis >}},
{{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}}).

#### Radial heat flux

For constant $K_{\mathrm c}$ the steady spherical conduction profile is $T=A+B/r$, whose radial flux $K_{\mathrm c}B/r^2$ times the face
area $\propto r^2$ is the same through every sphere. The code takes the radial flux through face $r_f$ between
centres $r_l<r_r$ as

$$
F^{(E)}_{r_f} = -\,K_{\mathrm c,f}\,\frac{T_r-T_l}{r_r-r_l}\,\frac{r_lr_r}{r_f^2} .
$$ {#eq-ch09-csdiffusion-radial}

For $T=A+B/r$, $T_r-T_l=B(r_l-r_r)/(r_lr_r)$, so $F^{(E)}_{r_f}=K_{\mathrm c,f}B/r_f^2$: exactly $-K_{\mathrm c}\partial_rT$ at $r_f$.
Times the face area, $r_f^2$ times the solid angle of the cell, it is the same on every radial face, and the
radial divergence vanishes. A prescribed wall temperature $T_w>0$ uses the same form between the wall and the first
centre ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}}).

The conductivity on that wall face is extrapolated from the two nearest cells, the wall cell $0$ and the next one,
linearly in position, which also holds on a stretched $x_1$:

1. *The weight.* With $h_0$ and $h_1$ [m] the radial widths of the two cells, $g=h_0/(h_0+h_1)$ [-].
2. *The extrapolation.* $K_{\mathrm c,w}=(1+g)K_{\mathrm c,0}-gK_{\mathrm c,1}$, and $K_{\mathrm c,0}$ instead when that is negative.
3. *Why it is linear in position.* The centres sit $h_0/2$ and $h_0+h_1/2$ from the wall. For $K_{\mathrm c}=a+br$ the
   step from centre 1 to centre 0 is $-b(h_0+h_1)/2$, and $g$ times it, $-bh_0/2$, is the step from centre 0 to the
   wall. So $K_{\mathrm c,w}$ is the wall value of a linear $K_{\mathrm c}$ on any widths.
4. *Equal widths.* $g=\tfrac12$, the $\tfrac32K_{\mathrm c,0}-\tfrac12K_{\mathrm c,1}$ of a uniform grid (`[C3]` of
   `stretched_x1_check.py`, @sec-ch09-viscosity).

The explicit operator and the implicit radial step (`radial_conduction_step`,
{{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::radial_conduction_step >}}) both use this $g$.

#### Angular heat flux

On the equiangular panel, with $X=\tan x_2$, $Y=\tan x_3$ and $D=1+X^2+Y^2$, the metric of the unit sphere in the two angles is
$\big[D^2(1+X^2)^{-1}(1+Y^2)^{-1}\big]^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}1+X^2&-XY\\-XY&1+Y^2\end{pmatrix}$, written in the
two angles. The matrix has determinant $(1+X^2)(1+Y^2)-X^2Y^2=D$, so its inverse is

$$
\mathcal G^{22}=\frac{D}{1+X^2},\qquad \mathcal G^{33}=\frac{D}{1+Y^2},\qquad \mathcal G^{23}=\frac{D\,XY}{(1+X^2)(1+Y^2)} .
$$

The unit normal of a face $x_2=$ const is $\nabla x_2/\lvert\nabla x_2\rvert$ with $\lvert\nabla x_2\rvert=\sqrt{\mathcal G^{22}}/r$,
so

$$
\hat{\mathbf n}_2\cdot\nabla T=\frac{\mathcal G^{22}\partial_2T+\mathcal G^{23}\partial_3T}{r\sqrt{\mathcal G^{22}}}
=\frac1r\Big(\sqrt{\mathcal G^{22}}\,\partial_2T+\frac{\mathcal G^{23}}{\sqrt{\mathcal G^{22}}}\,\partial_3T\Big),
$$

the expression of `heat` in the angular branch, with `gaa`, `gbb`, `gab` the three entries
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}}). The radius is orthogonal
to both panel axes, so no radial derivative enters a horizontal heat flux.

#### Block edges

A face on a block edge is computed by both blocks, each with its own one-sided stencil. The exchange sends each
side's outward flux times the face area; each side then replaces its face flux by the mean of its own and the
negated neighbour's, `0.5 * (f - sign * other / area)` (`share_fluxes`,
{{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp share_fluxes >}}). Both sides then hold the same flux with opposite
outward signs, so the face contributes equal and opposite amounts to the two cells, and momentum and energy are
conserved across the seam exactly up to round-off.

A mean of two fluxes does not couple two panels that are each piecewise constant, because both one-sided gradients
vanish. The code adds a symmetric interior penalty on the jump $\Delta q$[^rg-e6323cad5c0b] of the face traces (neighbour minus own):

$$
\mathbf F^{(\mathbf m)}_{\mathrm{pen}}=-\frac{2\bar\mu}{\Delta n_{\mathrm s}}\Big[\Delta\mathbf v+\tfrac13\hat{\mathbf n}(\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\Delta\mathbf v)\Big],\qquad
F^{(E)}_{\mathrm{pen}}=-\frac{2\bar K_{\mathrm c}}{\Delta n_{\mathrm s}}\Delta T+\bar{\mathbf v}\cdot\mathbf F^{(\mathbf m)}_{\mathrm{pen}},
$$ {#eq-ch09-csdiffusion-penalty}

added with the outward sign of each side, with $\bar\mu$, $\bar K_{\mathrm c}$ and $\bar{\mathbf v}$ the means of the two sides
and $\Delta n_{\mathrm s}$ the sum of the two centre-to-face normal distances ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp share_fluxes >}}).
The bracket is the Newtonian traction of a velocity jump spread over $\Delta n_{\mathrm s}$: for
$\nabla\mathbf v=\Delta\mathbf v\otimes\hat{\mathbf n}/\Delta n_{\mathrm s}$,
$\boldsymbol\Pi\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}=\mu[\Delta\mathbf v+\hat{\mathbf n}(\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\Delta\mathbf v)-\tfrac23\hat{\mathbf n}(\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\Delta\mathbf v)]/\Delta n_{\mathrm s}$,
which is $\mu$ times the bracket over $\Delta n_{\mathrm s}$; the penalty is twice that. Each side adds the same term with its own outward
sign, so the penalty is conservative too. On a smooth field the traces are cubic, so the jump is $O(h^4)$ of the
field and the penalty $O(h^3)$ (the code's comment on `weights`, {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp weights >}}).

#### Walls

The radial walls are reflecting. With `wall_velocity: stress-free` the wall traction keeps only its normal part,
$\mathbf t\leftarrow\hat{\mathbf n}(\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\mathbf t)$; with `no-slip` it is the traction of a velocity
that goes to zero at the wall over the half cell, $\mathbf t=\mu_f[\mathbf s+\tfrac13\hat{\mathbf n}(\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\mathbf s)]$ with
$\mathbf s=\mathbf v_c/(r_c-r_w)$. The wall face velocity is set to zero in both cases, so the viscous work through
a wall vanishes ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}}).

#### The tendency

The module subtracts $\Delta t$ times the `divergence` of the three flux arrays, converts the Cartesian momentum
tendency to contravariant components and lowers it with $g_{ab}$ to the covariant rows the solver stores
(`cs_cart_to_contra_`, `coord_vec_lower_`, {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}}).

#### The implicit radial heat step

With `implicit_radial: true` the explicit radial heat flux is set to zero and the radial conduction is solved
column by column instead ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::radial_conduction_step >}}). At
frozen density and the dry ideal-gas $c_v$, the energy of a column changes only through $T$, and the radial part of
the conduction is the linear system

$$
\mathsf M\,\frac{\mathrm dT}{\mathrm dt}=-\mathsf K\,T+\mathbf S,
$$ {#eq-ch09-csdiffusion-sdirk}

with $\mathsf M$ the diagonal of $\rho c_v$ times the radial volume measure $\Delta r\,(r_+^2+r_+r_-+r_-^2)/3$,
$\mathsf K$ the tridiagonal conductance matrix built from the face conductances $\bar K_{\mathrm c}\,r_lr_r/(r_r-r_l)$ of
@eq-ch09-csdiffusion-radial, and $\mathbf S$ the wall source when a wall temperature is given. It is advanced by the
two-stage singly diagonally implicit Runge–Kutta method with $b_{\mathrm{SD}}=1-1/\sqrt2$ (`gamma` in
`radial_conduction_step`, {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::radial_conduction_step >}}):

1. $(\mathsf M+b_{\mathrm{SD}}\Delta t\,\mathsf K)\,T_1=\mathsf MT^n+b_{\mathrm{SD}}\Delta t\,\mathbf S$;
2. $(\mathsf M+b_{\mathrm{SD}}\Delta t\,\mathsf K)\,T_2=\mathsf M\big[T^n+\tfrac{1-b_{\mathrm{SD}}}{b_{\mathrm{SD}}}(T_1-T^n)\big]+b_{\mathrm{SD}}\Delta t\,\mathbf S$.

Step 2 is the second stage $T_2=T^n+(1-b_{\mathrm{SD}})\Delta t\,f(T_1)+b_{\mathrm{SD}}\Delta t\,f(T_2)$ with
$f(T_1)=(T_1-T^n)/(b_{\mathrm{SD}}\Delta t)$ substituted from step 1. The method is second order, and L-stable
because its last stage is the solution. Both stages share one matrix, factored once by the Thomas algorithm. The
energy row gains $\rho c_v(T_2-T^n)$. $\mathsf K$ is a flux difference, so with insulating walls the column energy
is conserved. The solve throws when $T_2$ is not finite and positive.

*Exact and truncated.* Seam conservation, the rigid-rotation zero and the $T=A+B/r$ equilibrium are exact up to
round-off. Face values use the cubic through four cells, $O(h^4)$; face derivatives use its derivative, $O(h^4)$ on
the centred interior rows and $O(h^3)$ on the shifted edge rows and on the tangential derivatives at cell centres,
whose four cells are never centred. The measured order of the whole heat operator is in the Tests layer. The
radial step is second order in time, and it is split from the explicit step with a half step on each side.

*On a stretched $x_1$* (`geometry/x1f` or `cells/x1rat`), `weights` builds the $x_1$ rows on the actual radii: the
nodes are the four cell centres $x_{1,i}$ and the rows are evaluated at the faces $x_{1,i\pm1/2}$[^rg-6c8f7a42b6af] or at the centres,
with the scale $h=1$ because the nodes already carry lengths. The $x_2$ and $x_3$ rows, and every row of a uniform
$x_1$, keep the index-space weights. The cubic through four cells is then the cubic in $r$[^rg-c9fdf7ec5393], so value and derivative
keep the orders above on unequal widths; index-space weights on the same cells do not reproduce a cubic (`[C4]` of
`stretched_x1_check.py`: on five cells growing by a factor 1.3 the face value and derivative of a cubic are off
by $0$ and $1.0\times10^{-13}$ on the radii, and by $2.52\times10^{-3}$ and $1.87\times10^{-1}$ in index space).

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-csdiffusion-stencil shows which cells each face row uses along one direction of a block.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-csdiffusion-stencil
#| fig-cap: "Rows of the cubed-sphere diffusion stencil along one direction of a six-cell block. Each face (orange) is evaluated from the cubic through four interior cells (sky blue). Interior faces take the four cells centred on them; the two faces at each block edge and their neighbours take the four cells shifted inward (green labels), so no ghost cell is read. At an angular block edge (dashed) the neighbour computes the same face from its side, and the exchange makes the two sides carry one flux."
#| fig-alt: "Seven rows, one per face of a six-cell block, each showing six cells with four of them shaded and a marker on the face the row evaluates; the first two and last two rows have their shaded cells pushed against the block edge."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.figures.fig_csdiffusion_stencil import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Where things live: the seven fields of the operator ($T$, the Cartesian velocity and the Cartesian position) are
cell averages taken as centre values; face values, face derivatives and the face coefficient are point values at the
face centre; fluxes are face-averaged by multiplication with the face area in `divergence`. The operator reads the
interior cells of the block only. The face coefficient inside the block is the two-cell mean weighted by the $x_1$ widths,
$(h_rq_l+h_lq_r)/(h_l+h_r)$ for the cells $l$[^rg-adf81aa699d0] and $r$ of a radial face, and the plain average on $x_2$ and $x_3$ faces.
At every block edge it is the linear extrapolation $(1+g)q_0-gq_1$ from the two nearest cells with $g=h_0/(h_0+h_1)$,
$\tfrac32q_0-\tfrac12q_1$ on equal widths, falling back to $q_0$ when the extrapolation is negative. Angular block edges are joined by `share_fluxes`, which calls the scalar block exchange
four times, once per side, through one 12-channel buffer (outward flux, trace, coefficients and distance); radial
edges are walls. It runs in every stage of the explicit Runge–Kutta scheme, in the forcing loop
(@sec-ch09-framework). The implicit radial step runs as a half step at the start of stage 0, before the stage's
boundary fill and exchange, and as a half step after the last stage's averaging; a rejected step restores the state
from before the first half step (`begin_step`, `finish_step`, `restore_step`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).

Order of accuracy: the measured convergence of the heat operator on a degree-2 harmonic, the second-order
convergence of the radial step, the modal onset in a thin shell and the viscous operator on a stretched radial grid
are in the Tests layer; the viscous order on a uniform grid and the order through the full solver are **not measured**.

### Code

**A minimal input.** The diffusion block of `examples/cubed_sphere_convection.yaml`
({{< code examples/cubed_sphere_convection.yaml >}}), on a `gnomonic-equiangle` grid with the `cubed-sphere` layout,
`nb1` absent (one block in $x_1$) and reflecting radial walls:

```yaml
forcing:
  diffusion:
    dynamic: true           # nu_iso is mu [Pa s], kappa_iso a conductivity [W m^-1 K^-1]
    nu_iso: 0.003
    kappa_iso: 0.0105
    temperature_inner: 1.1  # K at the inner wall; 0 (default) leaves the wall insulating
    temperature_outer: 1.0
    wall_velocity: stress-free   # or no-slip
    implicit_radial: true   # radial conduction by the split SDIRK step; dry ideal gas only
```

`temperature_inner` and `temperature_outer` are the prescribed temperatures [K] of the inner and outer
$x_1$ walls; 0, the default, leaves a wall insulating. `wall_velocity` is the viscous condition at the radial
walls, `stress-free` (default) or `no-slip`. `implicit_radial` is a switch that moves the radial heat flux
into the split implicit step; default `false`.

**What is refused, and why.** All in `DiffusionImpl::reset` ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::reset >}})
unless stated.

1. *`implicit_radial` on another grid or EOS[^rg-a70646e99981]*: "[Diffusion] implicit_radial requires cubed sphere and dry ideal-gas
   EOS."; the frozen-$c_v$ linear system needs the dry ideal gas. A value other than `true`/`false` is refused by
   the parser ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. *A positive coefficient on a grid other than `cartesian` or `gnomonic-equiangle`*: "[Diffusion] Supported
   coordinates: cartesian, gnomonic-equiangle."
3. *A negative or non-finite wall temperature* (parser and `reset`), and *`wall_velocity` other than `stress-free`
   or `no-slip`*; `no-slip` on a Cartesian grid: "[Diffusion] The no-slip wall option requires gnomonic-equiangle."
4. *On the cubed sphere with a positive coefficient*: fewer than two ghosts, fewer than $\max(4,n_{\mathrm{ghost}})$
   interior cells in a direction, or a non-positive radius ("[Diffusion] Cubed sphere requires positive radii,
   nghost >= 2 and at least max(4, nghost) active cells per direction."): the stencil needs four interior cells; a
   layout other than `cubed-sphere` or more than one block in $x_1$ ("...requires cubed-sphere layout and nb1=1."):
   the radial walls and the radial solve are inside one block; and $x_1$ boundary names not starting with
   `reflecting` ("[Diffusion] Cubed sphere currently requires reflecting radial walls.").
5. *At run time*, the radial step refuses a non-finite or non-positive $\Delta t$ and a result that is not finite
   and positive ("...reduce dt."), and `restore_step` without a saved state
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::radial_conduction_step >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::restore_step >}}).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch09-csdiffusion-flux and @eq-ch09-csdiffusion-grad** (`forward_cubed_sphere`, per
direction `dir`[^rg-54e57b4e140f]):

```cpp
auto stress = cf[0] * (vg + vg.transpose(0, 1));
for (int j = 0; j < 3; ++j) stress[j][j] -= (2. / 3.) * cf[0] * div;
auto traction = (stress * normal.unsqueeze(0)).sum(1);
...
f.narrow(0, IVX, 3).copy_(-traction);
f[IPR].copy_(heat - vector_dot(face.narrow(0, 1, 3), traction));
```

`vg` is $\nabla\mathbf v$ of @eq-ch09-csdiffusion-grad, `cf[0]` the face $\mu$ and `cf[1]` the face $K_{\mathrm c}$, `normal` $\hat{\mathbf n}$, and `heat`
the conductive flux of @eq-ch09-csdiffusion-radial or of the angular formula.

| four-point weights | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp weights >}} | `weights` | |
| panel basis | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp basis >}} | `basis` | |
| fluxes and tendency | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward_cubed_sphere >}} | `forward_cubed_sphere` | |
| seam flux and penalty | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_cubed_sphere.cpp share_fluxes >}} | `share_fluxes` | |
| radial solve | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::radial_conduction_step >}} | `radial_conduction_step` | `implicit_radial` |
| split hooks | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::begin_step >}} | `begin_step`, `finish_step`, `restore_step` | `implicit_radial` |
| time-step bound | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::max_time_step >}} | `DiffusionImpl::max_time_step` | |

: Code map of the cubed-sphere viscosity and heat conduction. {#tbl-ch09-csdiffusion-code}

1. `DiffusionImpl::forward` checks the profiles, puts them on the state's device, and on `gnomonic-equiangle`
   returns `du` unchanged when both coefficients are zero and calls `forward_cubed_sphere` otherwise
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}).
2. `forward_cubed_sphere` packs $T$, the Cartesian velocity and the Cartesian position, and the coefficients $\mu$
   and $K_{\mathrm c}$ times the profiles, on the interior cells.
3. Per direction it interpolates the seven fields to the faces, differentiates them along the three index
   directions with `weights`, forms `vg`, corrects the face velocity, takes the face coefficient, the stress,
   `traction` and `heat`, applies the wall rules on radial faces, and stores the flux. For angular directions it
   keeps the two edge slabs of trace and normal for the exchange.
4. `share_fluxes` exchanges the edge fluxes and traces and adds @eq-ch09-csdiffusion-penalty.
5. The tendency is $-\nabla\cdot\mathbf F$, its momentum rows go to contravariant and then covariant components,
   and `du` gains $\Delta t$ times it.
6. `max_time_step` returns the bound of @eq-ch09-viscosity-dt times $1/8$ on the cubed sphere, a margin the code gives
   for the corrected non-orthogonal gradients and the $\tfrac43$ longitudinal viscous eigenvalue. With
   `implicit_radial` it returns instead $1/(16\sum_j\lambda_j)$, with $\lambda_1=\tfrac43\nu_{\max}/\Delta x_{1,\min}^2$
   and $\lambda_{2,3}=\tfrac43K_{\Delta t}/\Delta x_{j,\min}^2$, which leaves out the radial conduction
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::max_time_step >}}).
7. With `implicit_radial`, `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` calls `begin_step` at stage 0, then refills the boundaries
   and the ghost exchange, and `finish_step` after the last stage's averaging; `apply_redo` calls `restore_step`
   after it copies back the step-start state ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}},
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).

and 8 steps: ratios 4.43 and 4.16, slope 2.10: second order in time. `[C4]` The modal onset printed $Ra=652.25$ at $n=48$ and $658.89$ at $n=96$ against the thin-shell value
657.649, relative differences $-0.82\,\%$ and $+0.19\,\%$ within the 2 % tolerance. `[C5]` On the stretched faces the viscous test printed relative
$L_2$ errors $3.06\times10^{-3}$, $8.63\times10^{-4}$ and $2.18\times10^{-4}$ at 12, 24 and 48 cells per panel edge:
ratios 3.55 and 3.96, second order on widths up to 5.07 times apart. `stretched_radial_implicit_wall_k` and the
stretched and implicit arms of `radial_conductive_equilibrium` passed on CPU and CUDA in the same run.

**Evidence.** The numbers above come from the ctest runs in the footnote. **Coverage.** All cases run on CPU in double
precision; the two `cuda_*` cases compare CUDA with CPU; three cases run on two processes; the UCX two-GPU case
needs a build with UCX, two local processes and two visible devices; it skipped in the run above, which exposed one
device, and is **not run** here.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Reflecting radial walls, one block in $x_1$ and at least four interior cells per direction. The time step is $1/8$
of the Cartesian bound. Conduction acts on $T$. The implicit radial step needs the dry ideal gas.
:::

1. **One block in $x_1$, reflecting radial walls.** Refused otherwise at setup (Code, item 4). An $x_1$ seam or an
   open radial boundary has no flux rule here.
2. **Time step.** The explicit bound is the Cartesian one times $1/8$, a margin, not a derived stability limit; the
   bound with `implicit_radial` is likewise a stated factor. Neither is measured against the operator's spectrum on
   a production grid.
3. **Order.** The measured orders are those of the heat operator on one smooth harmonic and of the viscous operator
   on one stretched radial grid (`[C5]`); the viscous order on a uniform grid and the order through the solver are
   **not measured**.
4. **Conduction on $T$**, as in @sec-ch09-viscosity: a resting adiabat drifts.
5. **The implicit radial step** freezes density and uses the dry ideal-gas $c_v$ over the half step. It is split
   symmetrically, a half step before and a half step after the explicit step; the splitting error with the full
   solver is **not measured**.
6. **Untested combinations.** With an implicit hydrodynamic scheme, sedimentation or species: not run by any ctest
   listed here; see @sec-ch12-matrix.

[^rg-e6323cad5c0b]: $\Delta q$ — the change of $q$ over one RK stage, stated each time as "per stage" or "per step"; on a state variable in an implicit context write $\Delta^{\mathrm{stg}}\rho$ for the stage change and keep $\Delta\rho_i$ for the solved change of the row below; notation only; see @sec-appa
